audit.title: The Request Lifecycle

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong section leads: each state opens with a self-contained sentence ("This is the initial state of every new request in the manual flow"). The page lacks a top-level TL;DR/summary of all states before diving in.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean hierarchy (8 headings, 1 H1, max H3, 0 level skips per measured facts), consistent Trigger/What it means/Next Steps bullet pattern. A state machine with zero tables is the gap — the transitions belong in one liftable table.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Some good specifics (NAV TTL = 0, `3600` seconds for one hour), but measured facts show only 8 numerals, 0 with units. No timing, batch-window, or limit details beyond the TTL example.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Only 1 internal link (llms.txt), 0 external. No links to the DTA Request Management / Settlement contract docs, the states are named but not cross-linked to their reference pages.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good: NAV TTL is defined inline, and each state has a verbatim-liftable definition. Terminal states are explicitly labeled.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak: measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Nothing for an engine to parse for trust/freshness.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code or state enum shown. Acceptable for a pure concept page, but an agent gets no machine-consumable state list or enum values.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers the lifecycle end-to-end but only in concept-titled form. No troubleshooting/FAQ, no headings matching "how do I cancel", "why did my subscription fail", "what happens if NAV is stale".

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Product/entity names (DTA Request Management, Transfer Agent, Fund Distributor) are used consistently.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured conceptual page explaining the DTA request state machine, with crisp per-state definitions and consistent terminology. Its biggest strengths are prose clarity and answer-first section leads; its biggest weaknesses are zero machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates) and the absence of a state-transition table for a topic that is fundamentally tabular. Retrieval will also suffer because no section is phrased as the symptom/how-to questions developers actually ask ("why did my request fail", "can I cancel a request"). Honest verdict: solid content, under-optimized for both machine parsing and query matching.

recommendations.title: Add a state-transition summary table
recommendations.where: Directly under the intro, before "Manual processing lifecycle".
recommendations.issue: State machine described only in prose bullets; measured facts show 0 tables.
recommendations.change: Add a table with columns `State | Trigger | Next state(s) | Terminal?` covering Pending, Processing, Canceled, Processed, Failed — the single most liftable chunk for this page.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract transitions and build justified answers; a state machine is inherently tabular data currently locked in prose.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to phrased headings
recommendations.where: New short subsections or an FAQ near the end.
recommendations.issue: No section matches queries like "why did my request fail" or "can I cancel a request".
recommendations.change: Add H3s such as "How do I cancel a subscription request?" (answer: only in Pending/manual mode) and "Why did my request move to Failed?" (answer: failed settlement/compliance check). Reuse existing body text.
recommendations.why: Devs and agents query by symptom; concept-titled prose loses retrieval that question-phrased headings win.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` + canonical + dates
recommendations.issue: Measured facts: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified`, canonical URL, and `about` (DTA Request Management). Add a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust for citation.

recommendations.title: Cross-link named entities to their reference pages
recommendations.where: First mention of "DTA Request Management", "DTA Request Settlement", "Transfer Agent".
recommendations.issue: Only 1 internal link on the whole page; core entities are unlinked.
recommendations.change: Link each entity to its canonical concept/contract page on first use.
recommendations.why: Inline links to canonical sources raise credibility and let engines resolve entities and follow the doc graph.

recommendations.title: Add a top-of-page TL;DR
recommendations.issue: No single liftable summary distinguishing the two lifecycles.
recommendations.change: 2–3 sentence lead: "NAV TTL = 0 → manual batch processing with a Pending/cancel window; NAV TTL > 0 → automatic processing, no cancellation." State the canonical rule first.
recommendations.why: A crisp canonical statement is what engines lift verbatim and defends against skim/prior-based answers.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to the automatic flow
recommendations.issue: Only the `3600` example carries a unit; freshness/atomicity described qualitatively.
recommendations.change: State the TTL unit explicitly (seconds), the check condition (`now - lastNavUpdate ≤ NAV TTL`), and note the single-transaction atomicity.
recommendations.why: Quantitative, parameterized claims are among the highest-lift changes for source visibility.

antiPatterns: **Broken image reference:** `(Image: Image)` placeholder in the manual-processing section — a state diagram is referenced but renders as a non-descriptive placeholder; add real alt text or remove.
**Undated content:** no visible last-updated signal (confirmed by measured facts) — reduces freshness trust.
No keyword stuffing, marketing fluff, or unresolved cross-references detected; prose is clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already linked — good; ensure this page is enumerated in it and in the sitemap.
Site-level JSON-LD and freshness cadence are template concerns beyond this single page; fix at the docs-platform level.
CLI could pass raw `<head>` for a fuller metadata read — current run captured none, so head tags are unverified rather than confirmed absent.
